notes: Each Nano is plugged into its own mini breadboard straddling the centre gap (left-side pins in row b, right-side pins in row i). The exact columns are my assumption; the image draws no breadboard. Only the pins the circuit uses (A4, A5, 3V3 and GND) are listed as inserted.
I2C: A4 is SDA and A5 is SCL on both boards. Reader A5 joins writer A5 and reader A4 joins writer A4, through the bus strips on bb1 (columns 20 and 21 of the top bank).

Pull-ups: r1 runs from the SCL strip (20t) to the 3V3 strip (20b). r2 runs from the SDA strip (21t) to the same 3V3 strip (20b). Only the reader's 3V3 is wired, as in the image; the writer's 3V3 is unused.
GND of the two boards is joined by one jumper between the GND strips (14b) of the two breadboards.
Both boards are powered and programmed over USB; the USB cable type has no catalogue ports, so those edges have no port on the cable side.
The parts list says 10 jumper wires, but the image needs only 6, so only 6 are used.
